plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: A deciduous flowering cherry covered in clouds of delicate, slightly fragrant blossoms that appear before the leaves emerge. It is the iconic tree of hanami celebrations and is widely planted in parks and along waterways across temperate regions.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late March to mid-April in temperate Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Japan, Washington D.C. (USA), South Korea, and temperate parks worldwide
plants.funFact: The Yoshino cherry trees around Washington D.C.'s Tidal Basin were a gift from Tokyo in 1912, and their peak bloom date is tracked closely each year by the National Park Service.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers and blue-green strap-like leaves. It grows wild in woodlands and meadows of western Europe and is the ancestor of many garden daffodil cultivars.
plants.location: Western Europe (UK, France, Spain, Belgium) and naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: All parts of daffodils contain toxic alkaloids such as lycorine, and a compound from them, galantamine, is used in medicine to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A tall subtropical tree with fern-like foliage that bursts into masses of lavender-blue trumpet-shaped flowers. In the Southern Hemisphere, a second, lighter flowering sometimes occurs in autumn, while in places like Argentina and parts of Africa early blooms may appear.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the tropics and subtropics; sporadic autumn blooms in the Southern Hemisphere; main bloom September to November in the south
plants.location: Native to Argentina and Bolivia; cultivated in northern Australia, South Africa, India, and Mexico
plants.funFact: In Mexico City and parts of Pretoria, jacaranda trees carpet the streets in purple when they drop their flowers, creating a famous seasonal spectacle.

plants.name: Magnolia stellata
plants.description: A compact deciduous shrub or small tree bearing star-shaped flowers with many narrow, strap-like petals. The fragrant blooms open on bare branches in early spring and can be damaged by late frosts.
plants.location: Native to Japan; widely grown in gardens in the eastern United States, Europe, and temperate Asia
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants, having evolved before bees existed, and their flowers are thought to have been adapted for pollination by beetles.
